title: dependency-scan-variance-and-evidence-index-jun-2027
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working note documenting observed variance across our dependency scanners (internal runtime scanner, Snyk, OSSIndex) for the May–June 2027 sweep, proposed evidence-index schema for SIEM export, and recommended operational changes tied to RBAC v2 and patch SLA enforcement. Goal: reduce triage churn caused by duplicate/contradictory signals and ensure every vuln record exported to SIEM has tamper-evident evidence pointers that meet audit requirements.

Key findings (high level):
- Significant scanner variance: ~28% of findings are non-overlapping between any two scanners when normalized to pkg@version + vuln-id.
- False positive concentration: internal runtime scanner flags several container-only CVEs that static scanners don’t; Snyk reports many infra-as-code alerts not surfaced in runtime.
- Evidence gaps: ~40% of Snyk findings lack reproducible scan-artifact references (no build id, no SBOM fragment), making audit-proofing difficult.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: OSS and third-party dependency scans across services in Hosted and Dedicated accounts plus infra IaC scans. Does NOT include external pen-test or customer-reported vulns (handled by separate intake flow).
- Assumptions: all scanner outputs are ingested into the vuln-index pipeline; we can augment records with CI build metadata and immutable storage (artifacts bucket) for evidence.

Scanner comparison summary (May 15–Jun 1 sweep):
- Total unique raw findings across tools: 12,420
- Consolidated unique vuln keys (pkg@version + vuln id): 9,050
- Overlap: 72% of consolidated keys were reported by at least two tools; 28% single-source.
- High-frequency single-source patterns:
  * Internal runtime scanner: container CVEs flagged due to runtime libs (high noise in ephemeral container layers).
  * Snyk: IaC misconfig + open-source dependency transitive alerts, many with advisory references but missing SBOM context.
  * OSSIndex: broad coverage for older packages, sometimes outdated advisory mapping.

Impacts on triage and remediation:
- Duplicate tickets: triage team reports ~15% rework where a dependency was already being remediated but a second scanner created a new ticket due to different vuln id mapping.
- SLA drift: average time-to-patch for P2 issues increased by 1.4 days when cross-tool consolidation was missing.

Proposed evidence-index schema (flat fields for SIEM export and audit ingestion) – minimal required fields for each vuln event exported:
- vuln_key (string): normalized key pkg@version|vuln-id
- scan_source (string): e.g., snyk|ossindex|runtime-internal
- scan_timestamp (ISO8601 string)
- build_id (string): CI run id or container digest (if available)
- sbom_fragment (URL string): pointer to SBOM snapshot stored in artifacts-bucket
- evidence_url (URL string): signed pointer to raw scanner output JSON in object store
- proof_hash (string): sha256 of exported evidence bundle
- remediation_ticket (string): canonical jira ticket (if created)
- assigned_team (string)
- severity (string): normalized (critical|high|medium|low)
- first_seen (ISO8601)
- last_seen (ISO8601)
- resolution_state (string): new|triaged|fix-in-progress|fixed|wontfix
- rbac_viewer_role_required (string): minimal role having access to evidence (see RBAC section)

Notes on the schema: many fields above are optional in the pipeline but SIEM export MUST include proof_hash + evidence_url + vuln_key + scan_source to meet compliance auditors’ expectations. The final exported CSV/JSON should be flat key/value rows to ease SIEM ingestion.

RBAC v2 implications (evidence access and auditability):
- New role recommendation: evidence-viewer (read-only) scoped per-org and per-project. Purpose: allow CS/Legal to review proof bundle without granting ticket-assign or remediation rights.
- Evidence write path: only CI service account + vuln-ingest-service should be able to push evidence objects to artifacts-bucket; all writes generate an Audit Log entry (see audit schema below).
- Audit requirement: any change to resolution_state must include user/service principal and justification field (free text) in audit log entry; automated transitions (e.g., auto-closed by patch window) must record automation run id.

Audit log schema (fields to capture for compliance):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- principal (string): user/email or service account
- action (string): evidence_upload|state_change|ticket_link|rbac_change
- target_vuln_key (string)
- evidence_object (URL) || null
- justification (string) || null
- previous_state (string) || null
- new_state (string) || null
- run_id (string) || null (for automation)
- signature (string): HMAC or KMS-signed digest of event payload

SIEM export mapping (recommended field mapping to existing SIEM schema):
- vuln_key -> observable.id
- severity -> observable.severity
- scan_source -> vendor.name
- evidence_url -> observables.attachments[0].url (flattened in CSV)
- proof_hash -> observables.attachments[0].sha256
- remediation_ticket -> doc.reference
- audit_event -> saved as separate audit stream with event_id -> correlated by vuln_key

Patch SLA proposal (operational, per severity):
- Critical: 72 hours to mitigation plan, 7 days to patch in prod or approved compensating control. Escalation to SRE/Oncall and CISO inbox immediately.
- High: 7 days to mitigation plan, 30 days to patch or documented exception with compensating controls.
- Medium: 30 days to patch, tracked in monthly remediation sprint.
- Low: 90 days or scheduled in dependency bump cycles.

Remediation tracking and ticketing guidance (to reduce duplicate tickets across scanners):
- Canonical ticket creation rule: if vuln_key already exists in the vuln-index, append scanner evidence to existing ticket instead of creating a new one. Only create new ticket when vuln_key differs or the affected artifact (build_id/container digest) is different.
- Ticket labels: vuln.severity:<level>, vuln.source:<primary_scanner>, vuln.evidence:attached
- Auto-merge rules: when two tickets reference the same vuln_key, automation should merge them and keep the oldest remediation_ticket as canonical, preserving all evidence_url pointers.
- Auto-closure: tickets auto-closed only after proof_hash confirms fix in both build_id and production telemetry (where applicable).

Dependency review notes (manual observations from the sweep):
- Several transitive upgrades are blocked by pinned internal libs. Recommend a follow-up dependency-lift project to reduce pin density in core packages across 3 services (auth, routing, storage).
- Container base images are a recurring source of runtime-only CVEs. Short term: enforce base-image scan baseline and image digest pinning; medium term: move to smaller minimal images to reduce churn.

Operational changes recommended (short list):
1) Implement evidence-index fields in vuln-index pipeline and require proof_hash + evidence_url for SIEM export. (owner: Arjun, due: 2027-06-30)
2) Add evidence-viewer role to RBAC v2 proposals and ensure least-privilege for artifact reads. (owner: Sofia, due: 2027-06-20)
3) Triage automation update: consolidate by vuln_key before ticket create and attach scanner payloads instead of new tickets. (owner: Luca, due: 2027-07-10)
4) Patch SLA rollout: draft comms + SOC runbook for critical escalation path. (owner: Maya, due: 2027-06-18)

Open questions / discussion items:
- Which crypto approach for signature in audit events is acceptable to external auditors? (HMAC vs KMS-signed JWT).
- For SBOM fragments, do we require SPDX or CycloneDX canonicalization? Tradeoff: CycloneDX better for container layers, SPDX simpler text extraction.
- How to capture remediation footprint for multi-service fixes (single CVE patched via repo-level bump vs service-specific backports) in remediation_ticket field?

Appendix (quick examples):
Example vuln record (flat CSV row):
"vuln_key":"openssl@1.1.1k|CVE-2023-XXXXX","scan_source":"runtime-internal","scan_timestamp":"2027-05-18T14:03:21Z","build_id":"ci-12345","sbom_fragment":"https://artifacts.redwood.ai/sbom/ci-12345.json","evidence_url":"https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evidence/vuln-98765.json","proof_hash":"sha256:abcd...","remediation_ticket":"JIRA-SEC-4127","assigned_team":"platform-ops","severity":"high","first_seen":"2027-05-18T14:03:21Z","last_seen":"2027-06-01T07:22:10Z","resolution_state":"triaged","rbac_viewer_role_required":"evidence-viewer"

Action items recap (owners & due dates):
- Arjun: implement evidence-index export to SIEM (due 2027-06-30)
- Sofia: add evidence-viewer to RBAC v2 proposal + docs (due 2027-06-20)
- Luca: triage automation dedupe & ticket-merge rules (due 2027-07-10)
- Maya: patch SLA comms and SOC runbook (due 2027-06-18)

Notes to reviewers: this is an early working draft intended to capture scanner variance observations and make a minimal set of operational proposals that preserve auditability. Please comment with examples of specific tickets where duplicate creation caused SLA issues (tick refs in linked_artifacts help).
